findings.quote: Surveys list many repairs \citep{song2023learning,frenay2014classification}.
findings.evidence: Card: the survey reviews 62 robust training methods in five groups.

findings.quote: Surveys list many repairs \citep{song2023learning,frenay2014classification}.
findings.evidence: Abstract: reviews label noise-robust, cleansing and tolerant algorithms.

findings.quote: Loss correction and reweighting need an estimate of the noise rate or a clean validation set \citep{patrini2017making,ren2018learning}, and practitioners often have neither.
findings.evidence: Abstract: the loss corrections need the class corruption probabilities, which must be known or estimated.

findings.quote: Loss correction and reweighting need an estimate of the noise rate or a clean validation set \citep{patrini2017making,ren2018learning}, and practitioners often have neither.
findings.evidence: Abstract: the method minimizes the loss on a clean unbiased validation set to set example weights.

findings.quote: We revisit a simpler idea, cross-validated filtering of mislabeled data \citep{brodley1999identifying}, as a baseline that needs no side information.
findings.evidence: Abstract: classifiers act as noise filters to identify and eliminate mislabeled training instances. The sentence names the idea; cross-validation is explicit in brodley1996identifying.

findings.quote: Surveys group the field into robust losses, loss correction, example reweighting and sample selection \citep{song2023learning,frenay2014classification}.
findings.fix: The card says only that the survey has five groups and does not name them. Check the survey's section headings before listing the four families, or write 'Surveys group the methods into a handful of families'.

findings.quote: Surveys group the field into robust losses, loss correction, example reweighting and sample selection \citep{song2023learning,frenay2014classification}.
findings.fix: Frenay et al. group algorithms as label noise-robust, noise cleansing and noise-tolerant, not into these four families. Cite only song2023learning for the four-way grouping, and describe Frenay as 'robust, cleansing and tolerant algorithms'.

findings.quote: Robust losses change the objective \citep{zhang2018generalized}.
findings.evidence: Abstract: proposes noise-robust loss functions generalizing MAE and CCE as replacements for the training loss.

findings.quote: Loss correction needs the noise transition matrix or an estimate of it \citep{patrini2017making}, and reweighting needs a small clean validation set \citep{ren2018learning}.
findings.evidence: Abstract: corrections need the probability of each class being corrupted into another, and the paper also shows how to estimate these probabilities.

findings.quote: Loss correction needs the noise transition matrix or an estimate of it \citep{patrini2017making}, and reweighting needs a small clean validation set \citep{ren2018learning}.
findings.evidence: Abstract: only a small amount of clean validation data is available; weights come from minimizing loss on a clean unbiased validation set.

findings.quote: Co-teaching trains two deep networks that each pick small-loss samples for the other, and it needs the noise rate to set how many samples to keep \citep{han2018coteaching}.
findings.fix: The abstract confirms two networks that each select possibly clean data per mini-batch for the peer. 'Small-loss' and the dependence on the noise rate are body details not on the card. Check the paper (the keep-rate schedule uses the noise rate) or write 'each select possibly clean samples in a mini-batch for the other'.

findings.quote: Related selection methods learn a curriculum or fit a mixture to per-sample loss \citep{jiang2018mentornet,li2020dividemix}.
findings.evidence: Abstract: MentorNet learns a data-driven curriculum (sample weighting scheme) for the StudentNet.

findings.quote: Related selection methods learn a curriculum or fit a mixture to per-sample loss \citep{jiang2018mentornet,li2020dividemix}.
findings.evidence: Abstract: models the per-sample loss distribution with a mixture model to divide the data into clean and noisy sets.

findings.quote: Confident learning prunes samples using out-of-sample predicted probabilities and per-class thresholds, and it estimates the joint distribution of true and observed labels \citep{northcutt2021confident}.
findings.fix: The abstract backs pruning noisy data, probabilistic thresholds and estimating the joint distribution of noisy and uncorrupted labels. 'Out-of-sample predicted probabilities' and 'per-class' are body details. Check the paper or write 'prunes noisy samples using probabilistic thresholds and estimates the joint distribution of noisy and true labels'.

findings.quote: Classical noise filters remove the samples that cross-validated classifiers misclassify, then train on what remains \citep{brodley1996identifying,brodley1999identifying}.
findings.evidence: Abstract: n-fold cross validation passes the data through an ensemble filter, and only correctly classified instances go to the final learner.

findings.quote: Classical noise filters remove the samples that cross-validated classifiers misclassify, then train on what remains \citep{brodley1996identifying,brodley1999identifying}.
findings.evidence: Abstract: classifiers serve as noise filters that identify and eliminate mislabeled training instances, to improve accuracy of the learner trained on the cleaned data.

findings.quote: In the taxonomy of \citet{frenay2014classification} this is noise cleansing.
findings.evidence: Abstract: reviews label noise-robust, label noise cleansing and label noise-tolerant algorithms.

findings.quote: The MLP can fit flipped labels \citep{zhang2016understanding}.
findings.evidence: Abstract: networks trained with stochastic gradient methods easily fit a random labeling of the training data. The citation backs the general capacity claim, not the MLP result itself.

findings.quote: We did not compare with co-teaching \citep{han2018coteaching} or confident learning \citep{northcutt2021confident}, so we make no claim that the filter beats other noise-robust methods.
findings.evidence: The citation only names the method, Co-teaching (two networks teaching each other on noisy labels).

findings.quote: We did not compare with co-teaching \citep{han2018coteaching} or confident learning \citep{northcutt2021confident}, so we make no claim that the filter beats other noise-robust methods.
findings.evidence: The citation only names the method, confident learning (cleanlab).
